---
title: "GUI and settings"
description: "Give users a small, persistent settings surface."
---

Use `warden.GuiBuilder` to add settings and `warden.Config` to read saved values. Use stable, namespaced keys.

```lua
local WGG, warden = ...
local gui = warden.GuiBuilder:New()
local category = gui:Category("Warden Basic")
local general = category:Tab("General")
general:Checkbox({
  text = "Use cooldown",
  key = "wardenBasic.useCooldown",
  default = true
})
general:Slider({
  text = "Defensive health",
  key = "wardenBasic.defensiveHealth",
  min = 1,
  max = 100,
  step = 1,
  default = 35
})
```

```lua
if warden.Config:Read("wardenBasic.useCooldown", true) then
  spells.Cooldown:execute()
end
```

The framework owns window lifecycle and persistence. Packages should add controls, not create a second configuration window.
